text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

Given the normal coagulation and inflammatory markers, I suspect a structural anomaly like a meniscal cyst or plica syndrome, especially with the family history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the isolated swelling, normal coagulation and inflammatory workup, and the strong family history, this presentation is most consistent with a benign genetic connective tissue disorder causing joint laxity or recurrent effusions, such as Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome
